problem: Find the $x$-coordinates of the points of inflection for $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1).$
worked_solution:
For continuous, twice-differentiable functions, we can determine possible points of inflection by solving the equation ${f}^{″}(x)=0.$ However, we must be sure to check that the concavity does indeed change at whatever points we find. 

First, we calculate the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+1} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =\frac{2\cdot ({x}^{2}+1)-2x\cdot 2x}{({x}^{2}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2(1-{x}^{2})}{(1+{x}^{2})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we solve ${f}^{″}(x)=0,$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2(1-{x}^{2})}{(1+{x}^{2})^{2}} & =0 \\ 1-{x}^{2} & =0 \\ (1-x)(1+x) & =0 \\ x & =\pm 1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we need to check if the concavity changes at $x=-1$  and $x=1.$ So, we pick points around them, say $x=-2,$ $x=0$ and $x=2,$ and compute the sign of ${f}^{″}(x):$    

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(-2) & =\frac{2(1-(-2)^{2})}{(1+(-2)^{2})^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{6}{25}<0 \\ {f}^{″}(0) & =\frac{2(1-(0)^{2})}{(1+(0)^{2})^{2}} \\  & =2>0 \\ {f}^{″}(2) & =\frac{2(1-(2)^{2})}{(1+(2)^{2})^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{6}{25}<0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since the concavity changes at $x=-1$ and $x=1,$ we conclude that $x=-1$ and $x=1$ are indeed points of inflection.
